task: Find the most recent article on BBC News about archaeological discoveries and summarize the main findings and their significance.
answer: Found the most recent BBC News article on archaeological discoveries: 'Roman settlement dating back 2,000 years found under new-build estate' (published 2026-11-07, BBC Wales, https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/c6r7ydgl44z7o). Main findings: A 'very significant' Roman settlement, including a jewellery workshop, was discovered under a new-build housing estate in Mancot, Flintshire, north-east Wales, by Heneb (the trust for Welsh archaeology) during mining surveys. Dozens of artefacts were recovered - pottery, coins (one from emperor Commodus AD 177-192 and one of Constantine ~200 years later), brooches and lead moulds - making it one of the biggest Roman artefact collections in the county; the site possibly originated in the Iron Age and saw successive occupation. Significance: The find changes understanding of the area's history, showing local industry exploited rich metal resources to produce decorative brooches and commodities likely servicing the Roman city of Chester, with pottery suggesting trade as far as mainland Europe. It challenges the long-held idea of a poor relationship between Romans and the native population, and experts call it the beginning of what could be a long period of discoveries in north-east Wales. Artefacts will be conserved at the National Museum of Wales in Cardiff before public display, possibly at Mold Museum in 2027.
